questions.q: What does a convolutional kernel do differently from a fully-connected layer?
options: It slides a small, shared grid of weights across the input, reusing the same weights at every position
It connects every input pixel to every output neuron with its own weight
It processes the image one pixel at a time, carrying a hidden state forward
It removes the need for backpropagation
questions.explain: A CNN's kernel is a small set of weights reused at every position it slides over, which is far cheaper than connecting every pixel independently.

questions.q: In the lesson's 4x4 image example, why did the vertical-edge kernel produce different signs (+1 and -1) at different positions?
options: The kernel's weights changed between positions
The image had random noise added
It was a rounding error
The kernel responds to left-right contrast, and the image's contrast pattern flips between the top rows and the bottom rows
questions.explain: The same kernel was applied at each position; the output's sign flipped because the image itself has light-on-left pixels on top and light-on-right pixels on the bottom.

questions.q: What does an RNN carry forward from one step of a sequence to the next?
options: The original input, unchanged
A separate copy of the entire network
A hidden state summarizing everything read so far
The loss function
questions.explain: Each RNN step computes a new hidden state from the current input and the previous hidden state, carrying a running summary forward.

questions.q: What is the main bottleneck of an RNN's step-by-step design?
options: It cannot be trained with gradient descent
It requires a convolutional kernel
It has no activation function
Information from early in a long sequence can fade by the time later steps are reached, and steps cannot be computed in parallel
questions.explain: Because each step depends on the previous one's hidden state, RNNs process sequentially (no parallelism) and long-range information can get compressed away.

questions.q: In one sentence, what does a transformer's self-attention replace the RNN's hidden state with?
options: A convolutional kernel applied to text
Every token directly looking at every other token in the sequence at once, instead of passing information step by step
A larger hidden state that never forgets anything
A random sampling of tokens
questions.explain: Self-attention lets every position attend to every other position directly and in parallel, removing the RNN's step-by-step bottleneck — the full topic of lesson 21.
